newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade rises 0.6 pct in Jan-Aug yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade rises 0.6 pct in Jan-Aug yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's trade with China grew only 0.6 percent to US$14.02 billion in the first eight months of 1996 over the same period last year, the state-owned Central News Agency said on Friday.
Taiwan's exports to China rose 1.9 percent to $12.04 billion from a year earlier, while imports slid 6.7 percent to $1.986 billion, the agency quoted the Board of Foreign Trade as saying.

The board attributed the recent sluggish growth to a reduction in China export rebate tax rate in January, causing Taiwanese makers in China to advance their exports ahead of the change. The cut also led to a slowdown in Taiwan's processing material exports to China.
In August alone, exports to China rose 14.2 percent to $1.58 billion from a year ago due to China's lowering banks' prime lending rates, the agency said.
Imports from China in August rose 8.0 percent to $267 million, the first rise after six straight months of declines, following an easing of imports restrictions on China goods in July.
During the January-August period, Taiwan enjoyed a trade surplus of $10.05 billion with China, up a year-on-year 3.8 percent, it said.

Beijing, which has considered Taiwan a renegade province since the Chinese civil war separated them in 1949, held war games in the Taiwan Strait ahead of the island's presidential election on March 23 to warn voters not to drop the pledge to reunify with China.
Officials have said the war games made Taiwanese less willing to invest in mainland.
Taiwan bans direct contact with China. All trade with China must be conducted through a third region, mostly Hong Kong. Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested more than $20 billion in China.
